I am a 49-year-old farmer in Quzhou, and I have farmed these fields for 25 years. I did not go far in school, but I know my land. My family has five people, and some of them work in town, so labor is tight at harvest and planting. I have 90 mu total, a well for irrigation, and I rely on what I have seen work year after year.

This year, I will put **80 mu into my wheat–maize rotation** and keep **10 mu for stevia**, which the buyer comes to collect every autumn.

For **winter wheat** on those 80 mu: I will buy improved seed from the county supply shop—the kind that has done well here, not traditional seed that risks poor germination. After the maize comes off, I will use the rotary tiller to prepare a fine seedbed. I will apply nitrogen at about 18 kg per mu (base dressing plus urea top-dress at jointing), phosphorus at 7 kg per mu, and potassium at 5 kg per mu. I will irrigate four times: before winter to help it survive the cold, at jointing, at booting, and during grain filling. Two pesticide sprays—one herbicide early and one fungicide when the weather warms. I expect around 500 kg per mu if frost and drought do not hit hard.

For **summer maize** on the same 80 mu: I will plant hybrid seed, absolutely. Everyone here uses hybrid maize now; the old types cannot compare. Because the season is short after wheat harvest and my hands are few, I will use no-tillage direct seeding to save time and fuel. Fertilizer will be 16 kg nitrogen per mu, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium. I will irrigate three times—once if it is dry after planting, then at the big-flare stage, and once at tasseling/silking. Two pesticide applications: a herbicide with planting and an insecticide later. I hope for 550 kg per mu.

For **stevia** on 10 mu: I will plant improved seedlings in spring once frost danger is past. Stevia is my cash crop, but it is fussy. I will rotary-till the beds to make them fine and level. It needs plenty of water, so I will irrigate five times through the season. Fertilizer will be 12 kg nitrogen per mu, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium to keep the leaves green and sweet. Three pesticide sprays, because leaf miners and caterpillars love it. I expect about 200 kg of dry leaf per mu.

Why? Because the wheat and maize give me grain I can sell or store, and the double cropping uses my good land fully. No-till maize saves my back and my time when labor is short. The stevia gives cash income that grain prices alone cannot match. I have the well, so I will use water when the crops need it—I have learned that skipping irrigation costs more in lost yield than the electricity bill.
